brief: Copy six words in the original read/write order, including overlapping spans.
decl: std::span<std::byte,24> copy_words24(std::span<std::byte,24> destination, std::span<const std::byte,24> source);
notes: Original bytes and execution establish argument widths and access order.
Spans are host byte views; original 32-bit address identities are explicit where needed.
The original leaves the destination address in EAX; the host returns its span and compares pointer identity.

bookkeeping.scope: Complete original body on supplied scalar state and valid byte spans. Copy cases include overlapping and unaligned views with the original read/write order.
bookkeeping.supported_domain: Valid fixed-size byte spans, including tested unaligned overlap. Native copies preserve the machine instruction read/write order rather than snapshot or generic byte-copy semantics.
bookkeeping.acceptance: Met: 39 synthetic original-execution cases matched bit-exact by MSVC and Zig/Clang runners. See docs/recovery/record-stack.md.
